review.title: Theory of Star Formation
review.journal: Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics

sources.authors: Shu, Frank H.; Adams, Fred C.; Lizano, Susana
sources.journal: Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics
sources.title: Star Formation in Molecular Clouds: Observation and Theory
sources.boundary: Established the classic theoretical framework of isolated, magnetically regulated inside-out core collapse.

sources.authors: Mac Low, Mordecai-Mark; Klessen, Ralf S.
sources.title: Control of star formation by supersonic turbulence
sources.boundary: Consolidated the paradigm shift toward supersonic turbulence as the primary regulator of molecular cloud fragmentation.

sources.authors: Kennicutt, Robert C., Jr.
sources.title: The Global Schmidt Law in Star-forming Galaxies
sources.boundary: Provided the canonical empirical calibration of the surface density scaling law for galactic star formation.

sources.authors: Salpeter, Edwin E.
sources.title: The Luminosity Function and Stellar Evolution.
sources.boundary: Defined the foundational high-mass power-law slope of the initial mass function.

sources.authors: Kroupa, Pavel
sources.title: The Initial Mass Function of Stars: Evidence for Uniformity in Variable Systems
sources.boundary: Parameterized the multi-part power-law functional form of the universal stellar IMF down to the brown dwarf regime.

sources.authors: Chabrier, Gilles
sources.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific
sources.title: Galactic Stellar and Substellar Initial Mass Function
sources.boundary: Established the standard lognormal parameterization for the low-mass end of the IMF.

sources.authors: Alves, J.; Lombardi, M.; Lada, C. J.
sources.title: The mass function of dense molecular cores and the origin of the IMF
sources.boundary: Measured the core mass function of the Pipe Nebula utilizing dust extinction, establishing a morphological match to the IMF offset by a 30% efficiency factor.

sources.authors: Lada, Charles J.; Lada, Elizabeth A.
sources.journal: Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics
sources.title: Embedded Clusters in Molecular Clouds
sources.boundary: Consolidated observations demonstrating that the vast majority of stars form in clustered environments rather than in isolation.

sources.authors: Krumholz, Mark R.; McKee, Christopher F.
sources.title: A General Theory of Turbulence-regulated Star Formation, from Spirals to Ultraluminous Infrared Galaxies
sources.boundary: Formulated an analytic framework predicting the star formation rate based on the lognormal density PDF of supersonic isothermal turbulence.

sources.authors: Padoan, Paolo; Nordlund, Åke
sources.title: A Super-Alfvénic Model of Dark Clouds
sources.boundary: Demonstrated via MHD simulations that molecular clouds exhibit super-Alfvénic turbulence and weak mean magnetic fields, challenging ambipolar diffusion models.

sources.authors: McKee, Christopher F.
sources.title: Photoionization-regulated Star Formation and the Structure of Molecular Clouds
sources.boundary: Modeled star formation rates driven by ambipolar diffusion where the ionization fraction is maintained by UV photoionization.

sources.authors: Zinnecker, Hans; Yorke, Harold W.
sources.journal: Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics
sources.title: Toward Understanding Massive Star Formation
sources.boundary: Synthesized theoretical challenges of high-mass star formation, specifically focusing on radiation pressure and accretion dynamics.

sources.authors: Solomon, P. M.; Rivolo, A. R.; Barrett, J.; Yahil, A.
sources.title: Mass, Luminosity, and Line Width Relations of Galactic Molecular Clouds
sources.boundary: Established the fundamental scaling relations (Larson's Laws) for Galactic GMCs using CO emission.

sources.authors: Elmegreen, Bruce G.
sources.title: Star Formation in a Crossing Time
sources.boundary: Observational-timescale argument for completion in one or a few crossing times; not a 1993 H2-transition paper.

sources.authors: Bate, Matthew R.; Bonnell, Ian A.; Bromm, Volker
sources.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
sources.title: The formation of a star cluster: predicting the properties of stars and brown dwarfs
sources.boundary: Conducted hydrodynamic simulations of cluster formation, demonstrating competitive accretion and dynamical ejections forming brown dwarfs.

sources.authors: McKee, Christopher F.; Tan, Jonathan C.
sources.title: The Formation of Massive Stars from Turbulent Cores
sources.boundary: Proposed the Turbulent Core model for massive star formation, arguing for rapid monolithic collapse in highly pressurized, turbulent environments.

sources.authors: Bonnell, I. A.; Bate, M. R.; Clarke, C. J.; Pringle, J. E.
sources.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
sources.title: Competitive accretion in embedded stellar clusters
sources.boundary: Competitive accretion model; depends on shared cluster potential and gas reservoir.

sources.authors: Larson, R. B.
sources.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
sources.title: Turbulence and star formation in molecular clouds.
sources.boundary: Identified the empirical scaling relations connecting velocity dispersion to the spatial scale of molecular clouds.

sources.authors: Larson, R. B.
sources.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
sources.title: Towards understanding the stellar initial mass function
sources.boundary: not usable

sources.authors: Krumholz, Mark R.; Klein, Richard I.; McKee, Christopher F.
sources.title: Radiation-Hydrodynamic Simulations of Collapse and Fragmentation in Massive Protostellar Cores
sources.boundary: Three-dimensional radiation-hydrodynamic setup and resolution bound the radiation-instability result.

sources.authors: Tomisaka, Kohji; Ikeuchi, Satoru; Nakamura, Takashi
sources.title: Equilibria and Evolutions of Magnetized, Rotating, Isothermal Clouds. II. The Extreme Case: Nonrotating Clouds
sources.boundary: Analytically determined the geometric coefficient for the critical mass-to-flux ratio of centrally condensed clouds.

sources.authors: Nakano, Takenori
sources.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
sources.title: Influence of Magnetic Fields on Sequential Formation of Subgroups in OB Associations
sources.boundary: Derived the critical magnetic mass-to-flux ratio for an infinite cold sheet.

sources.authors: McKee, Christopher F.; Tan, Jonathan C.
sources.title: Massive star formation in 100,000 years from turbulent and pressurized molecular clouds
sources.boundary: Established timescale and column density constraints for the rapid formation of massive stars.

sources.authors: Miller, G. E.; Scalo, J. M.
sources.title: The Initial Mass Function and Stellar Birthrate in the Solar Neighborhood
sources.boundary: Introduced the lognormal functional fit for the low-mass regime of the observed stellar mass distribution.

sources.authors: Muench, A. A., Lada, E. A., Lada, C. J., & Alves, J.
sources.title: The Luminosity and Mass Function of the Trapezium Cluster from a Deep Infrared Imaging Survey
sources.boundary: not usable

sources.authors: Motte, F.; Andre, P.; Neri, R.
sources.title: The initial conditions of star formation in the rho Ophiuchi main cloud: wide-field millimeter continuum mapping
sources.boundary: One of the first sub-millimeter studies mapping the dense core mass function, revealing its structural similarity to the IMF.

sources.authors: Testi, Leonardo; Sargent, Anneila I.
sources.title: Star Formation in Clusters: A Survey of Compact Millimeter-Wave Sources in the Serpens Core
sources.boundary: Utilized mm-wave interferometry to trace dust condensations, confirming a Salpeter-like mass spectrum for prestellar cores.

sources.authors: Beuther, Henrik; Schilke, Peter
sources.title: Fragmentation in MassiveStar Formation
sources.boundary: Captured high-resolution observations of massive dense cores, probing the initial fragmentation conditions for clustered star formation.

sources.authors: Zuckerman, B.; Palmer, P.
sources.journal: Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics
sources.title: Radio radiation from interstellar molecules.
sources.boundary: Identified the fundamental gas depletion time discrepancy, noting the observed SFR is drastically lower than the free-fall collapse rate.

sources.authors: Williams, Jonathan P.; McKee, Christopher F.
sources.title: The Galactic Distribution of OB Associations in Molecular Clouds
sources.boundary: Quantified the star formation efficiency in Milky Way GMCs, concluding it is regulated to be inefficient per crossing time.

sources.authors: Mouschovias, T. C.
sources.title: Magnetic braking, ambipolar diffusion, cloud cores, and star formation: Natural length scales and masses
sources.boundary: not usable

sources.authors: Mouschovias, T. C., & Ciolek, G. E.
sources.journal: The Origin of Stars and Planetary Systems
sources.title: Magnetic Fields and Star Formation
sources.boundary: not usable

sources.authors: Padoan, Paolo
sources.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
sources.title: Supersonic turbulent flows and the fragmentation of a cold medium
sources.boundary: Suggested an early analytic framework relating the turbulent lognormal density field to star formation efficiencies.

sources.authors: Wong, Tony; Blitz, Leo
sources.title: The Relationship between Gas Content and Star Formation in Molecule-rich Spiral Galaxies
sources.boundary: Analyzed extragalactic gas depletion times, extending the Kennicutt-Schmidt constraints specifically to molecule-dominated regions.

sources.authors: Fukui, Y., Mizuno, N., Yamaguchi, R., et al.
sources.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
sources.title: A Survey of Giant Molecular Clouds in the Magellanic Clouds
sources.boundary: not usable

sources.authors: Engargiola, G.; Plambeck, R. L.; Rosolowsky, E.; Blitz, L.
sources.title: Giant Molecular Clouds in M33. I. BIMA All-Disk Survey
sources.boundary: Provided robust measurements of GMC properties and internal turbulence within a local group spiral galaxy.

sources.authors: Papaloizou, J. C. B., & Lin, D. N. C.
sources.journal: Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics
sources.title: Theory of Accretion Disks I: Angular Momentum Transport Processes
sources.boundary: not usable

sources.authors: Stone, J. M.; Gammie, C. F.; Balbus, S. A.; Hawley, J. F.
sources.title: Transport Processes in Protostellar Disks
sources.boundary: Detailed the application of the Magneto-Rotational Instability (MRI) to angular momentum transport in protostellar environments.

sources.authors: Stahler, S. W.; Shu, F. H.; Taam, R. E.
sources.title: The evolution of protostars. I - Global formulation and results
sources.boundary: Formulated the early accretion physics linking the free-fall collapse rate of a core to the radius and luminosity of a protostar.

sources.authors: Mestel, L.; Spitzer, L., Jr.
sources.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
sources.title: Star formation in magnetic dust clouds
sources.boundary: Pioneered the concept of ambipolar diffusion as a mechanism to shed magnetic flux during cloud collapse.

sources.authors: Padoan, Paolo; Nordlund, Åke
sources.title: The Stellar Initial Mass Function from Turbulent Fragmentation
sources.boundary: Derives a core-mass spectrum from an isothermal turbulent density field; power spectrum, MHD jump, and collapse assumptions apply.

sources.authors: Ostriker, Eve C.; Gammie, Charles F.; Stone, James M.
sources.title: Kinetic and Structural Evolution of Self-gravitating, Magnetized Clouds: 2.5-dimensional Simulations of Decaying Turbulence
sources.boundary: 2.5-D isothermal periodic simulations; collapse and decay times depend on magnetization, Jeans number, and setup.

sources.authors: Li, P. S.; Norman, Michael L.; Mac Low, Mordecai-Mark; Heitsch, Fabian
sources.title: The Formation of Self-Gravitating Cores in Turbulent Magnetized Clouds
sources.boundary: Super-Alfvénic isothermal ZEUS-MP simulations; core statistics and collapse rates are resolution/initial-condition dependent.

sources.authors: Stone, James M.; Ostriker, Eve C.; Gammie, Charles F.
sources.title: Dissipation in Compressible Magnetohydrodynamic Turbulence
sources.boundary: Forced/decaying periodic MHD simulations show crossing-time-scale dissipation; no direct cloud-lifetime measurement.

sources.authors: Mac Low, Mordecai-Mark; Klessen, Ralf S.; Burkert, Andreas; Smith, Michael D.
sources.title: Kinetic Energy Decay Rates of Supersonic and Super-Alfvénic Turbulence in Star-Forming Clouds
sources.boundary: Isothermal decaying-turbulence simulations; driving requirement follows from model decay, not an observed driver identity.

sources.authors: Crutcher, Richard M.
sources.title: Magnetic Fields in Molecular Clouds: Observations Confront Theory
sources.boundary: Compilation of 27 sensitive Zeeman measurements; projection, tracer, nondetections, and geometry bound mass-to-flux inference.

sources.authors: Klessen, Ralf S.
sources.title: The Formation of Stellar Clusters: Mass Spectra from Turbulent Molecular Cloud Fragmentation
sources.boundary: Hydrodynamic self-gravitating models vary driving scale; simulated core spectra are not a one-to-one IMF prediction.

sources.authors: Larson, Richard B.
sources.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
sources.title: Thermal physics, cloud geometry and the stellar initial mass function
sources.boundary: Links characteristic mass to gas-dust thermal transition and geometry; metallicity/background assumptions apply.

sources.authors: Mouschovias, Telemachos Ch.; Tassis, Konstantinos; Kunz, Matthew W.
sources.title: Observational Constraints on the Ages of Molecular Clouds and the Star Formation Timescale: Ambipolar-Diffusion-controlled or Turbulence-induced Star Formation?
sources.boundary: Reinterprets age and linewidth data in an ambipolar-diffusion framework; contested model comparison, not consensus measurement.

sources.authors: Bonnell, Ian A.; Bate, Matthew R.; Zinnecker, Hans
sources.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
sources.title: On the formation of massive stars
sources.boundary: Cluster-mediated accretion/merger argument under dense-environment assumptions; not universal massive-star pathway.

sources.authors: Matzner, Christopher D.; McKee, Christopher F.
sources.title: Efficiencies of Low-Mass Star and Star Cluster Formation
sources.boundary: Analytic protostellar-outflow model predicts core/clump efficiencies; massive-star destructive feedback is excluded.
